text: Which of the following is the SI unit of electric current?
explanation: The SI unit of electric current is the Ampere (A), named after André-Marie Ampère. Volt is the unit of potential difference, Ohm is the unit of resistance, and Watt is the unit of power.

text: A physical quantity that has both magnitude and direction is called a
explanation: A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction (e.g. velocity, force). A scalar quantity has only magnitude (e.g. speed, mass).

text: The resultant of two vectors of magnitudes 3 N and 4 N acting at right angles to each other is
explanation: Using the Pythagorean theorem: R = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 N.

text: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
explanation: Temperature has only magnitude and no direction, making it a scalar. Velocity, displacement and weight all have direction and are vectors.

text: The distance covered per unit time is called
explanation: Speed is the rate of change of distance with time. Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time and includes direction.

text: A car starts from rest and reaches a velocity of 20 m/s in 5 seconds. Its acceleration is
explanation: Acceleration = (v - u)/t = (20 - 0)/5 = 4 m/s². Since it starts from rest, u = 0.

text: Which equation of motion correctly relates displacement, initial velocity, time and acceleration?
explanation: The equation s = ut + ½at² gives displacement in terms of initial velocity (u), time (t) and acceleration (a). The others relate to velocity and force.

text: Newton's first law of motion is also known as the law of
explanation: Newton's first law states that a body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force. This tendency to resist change in motion is called inertia.

text: The weight of a body of mass 5 kg on Earth where g = 10 m/s² is
explanation: Weight W = mg = 5 × 10 = 50 N. Weight is the gravitational force acting on a mass.

text: Which of the following is the correct statement of Newton's third law?
optionA: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
optionC: A body remains at rest unless acted upon
optionD: Momentum is conserved in all collisions
explanation: Newton's third law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. Forces always occur in pairs.

text: A force of 20 N acts on a body of mass 4 kg. The acceleration produced is
explanation: From Newton's second law, a = F/m = 20/4 = 5 m/s².

text: The work done by a force of 10 N moving a body through 5 m in the direction of the force is
explanation: Work = Force × distance = 10 × 5 = 50 J. Work is done when a force causes displacement in its own direction.

text: The energy possessed by a body due to its position is called
explanation: Gravitational potential energy is the energy stored in an object due to its height above a reference point. KE is due to motion.

text: A body of mass 2 kg is moving at 10 m/s. Its kinetic energy is
Power is defined as the
explanation: Power is the rate at which work is done (or energy is transferred). P = W/t. It can also be expressed as P = Fv.

text: A machine does 500 J of work in 10 seconds. Its power output is
explanation: Power P = W/t = 500/10 = 50 W.

text: Which principle states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed but can be converted from one form to another?
explanation: The law of conservation of energy is a fundamental principle in physics. Energy changes form but the total amount remains constant.

text: The efficiency of a machine is defined as
optionA: input work divided by output work
optionB: output work divided by input work multiplied by 100%
optionC: output force divided by input force
explanation: Efficiency = (useful output work / total input work) × 100%. A perfect machine would have 100% efficiency but this is impossible due to friction.

text: Which of the following best describes pressure?
explanation: Pressure is defined as force per unit area: P = F/A. Its SI unit is the Pascal (Pa) which equals N/m².

text: Archimedes' principle states that a body immersed in a fluid experiences an upthrust equal to the
explanation: Archimedes' principle: the upthrust (buoyant force) on a body equals the weight of fluid it displaces. This explains why objects float or sink.

text: A body floats in a liquid when its weight is
explanation: For a body to float, the upthrust (weight of fluid displaced) must exactly equal the weight of the body. This is the law of flotation.

text: Pascal's principle states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is
optionC: absorbed by the walls of the container
explanation: Pascal's principle: pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions throughout the fluid. This is the basis of hydraulic machines.

text: The SI unit of pressure is
explanation: The SI unit of pressure is the Pascal (Pa). 1 Pa = 1 N/m². Atmospheric pressure is approximately 101,325 Pa.

text: The number of complete oscillations a wave makes per second is called its
explanation: Frequency is the number of complete oscillations (cycles) per second, measured in Hertz (Hz). Period is the time for one complete oscillation.

text: The relationship between wave speed (v), frequency (f) and wavelength (λ) is
explanation: The wave equation is v = fλ, where v is wave speed in m/s, f is frequency in Hz, and λ is wavelength in m.

text: Which of the following types of wave requires a material medium for transmission?
explanation: Sound is a mechanical (longitudinal) wave that requires a medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel through. Electromagnetic waves like light can travel through a vacuum.

text: The distance between two successive crests of a transverse wave is called
explanation: Wavelength is the distance between two successive crests (or troughs) in a transverse wave, or between two successive compressions in a longitudinal wave.

text: A wave has a frequency of 200 Hz and a wavelength of 1.5 m. What is its speed?
Which of the following is a longitudinal wave?
explanation: In longitudinal waves, particles vibrate parallel to the direction of energy propagation. Sound waves are longitudinal. Transverse waves (e.g. light, water waves) have particles vibrating perpendicular to propagation.

text: The pitch of a sound is determined by its
explanation: Pitch is the human perception of frequency. A high-frequency sound has a high pitch; a low-frequency sound has a low pitch.

text: The loudness of a sound depends on its
explanation: Loudness (volume) depends on the amplitude of the sound wave. Larger amplitude means more energy and a louder sound.

text: The speed of sound in air at 0°C is approximately
explanation: The speed of sound in air at room temperature is approximately 340 m/s (and about 331 m/s at 0°C). It is much slower than the speed of light.

text: The phenomenon by which sound bounces back after hitting a hard surface is called
explanation: An echo is the reflection of sound. For a distinct echo, the reflecting surface must be at least 17 m away from the source (since the ear needs at least 0.1 s to distinguish the echo).

text: Resonance in sound occurs when the natural frequency of a body
optionB: is equal to the forcing frequency
explanation: Resonance occurs when a body is made to vibrate at its own natural frequency by an external force of the same frequency, resulting in maximum amplitude.

text: The bending of light as it passes from one medium to another is called
explanation: Refraction is the change in direction (and speed) of light as it passes from one optical medium to another with different optical densities.

text: Which law states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection?
explanation: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, and the incident ray, reflected ray and normal all lie in the same plane.

text: The critical angle is the angle of incidence in the denser medium for which the angle of refraction is
explanation: The critical angle is the specific angle of incidence (in the denser medium) that produces an angle of refraction of 90°. Beyond this angle, total internal reflection occurs.

text: A concave lens is also called a
explanation: A concave (diverging) lens causes parallel rays of light to spread out as if coming from a virtual focal point. A convex (converging) lens brings parallel rays to a real focal point.

text: The phenomenon responsible for the formation of a rainbow is
explanation: A rainbow forms when sunlight is refracted and dispersed (split into its component colours) by raindrops. Each colour bends at a slightly different angle due to different refractive indices.

text: The refractive index of glass is 1.5. What is the critical angle?
explanation: sin(C) = 1/n = 1/1.5 = 0.667. C = sin⁻¹(0.667) ≈ 41.8°. Total internal reflection occurs at angles greater than this.

text: The conventional direction of electric current flow is
explanation: By convention, current flows from the positive terminal to the negative terminal of a battery (opposite to the actual flow of electrons, which move from negative to positive).

text: Ohm's law states that the current through a conductor is
optionC: directly proportional to the voltage at constant temperature
explanation: Ohm's law: V = IR, meaning current (I) is directly proportional to voltage (V) at constant temperature. Resistance (R) is the constant of proportionality.

text: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. Their combined resistance is
Two resistors of 4 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in series. Their total resistance is
explanation: For series connection, total resistance = R₁ + R₂ = 4 + 6 = 10 Ω.

text: The electrical energy consumed by a device of power 100 W operating for 2 hours is
explanation: Energy = Power × time = 100 W × 2 h = 200 Wh (or 0.2 kWh, which is 0.2 units of electricity).

text: A magnetic field is produced around a wire whenever
optionA: a static charge is placed on it
explanation: A current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field around it. This is the basis of electromagnetism, discovered by Oersted.

text: The direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor is given by
explanation: The right-hand grip rule: if you grip the wire with your right hand with the thumb pointing in the direction of current, the curled fingers indicate the direction of the magnetic field.

text: Electromagnetic induction is the process by which
optionB: a changing magnetic field induces an EMF
explanation: Electromagnetic induction (Faraday's law): a changing magnetic flux through a conductor induces an electromotive force (EMF) in that conductor.

text: Lenz's law states that the induced EMF is in a direction that
explanation: Lenz's law is a consequence of the law of conservation of energy. The induced current creates a magnetic field that opposes the change in flux that produced it.

text: A transformer steps up voltage by a factor of 10. If the primary has 100 turns, the secondary has
explanation: Ns/Np = Vs/Vp. If the voltage steps up by 10, turns ratio = 10. Ns = 10 × 100 = 1000 turns.

text: Fleming's left-hand rule is used to determine the direction of force on a
optionA: charged particle in an electric field
optionB: current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
explanation: Fleming's left-hand rule (motor rule): the thumb, index finger and middle finger of the left hand represent the direction of force (motion), magnetic field, and current respectively.

text: The phenomenon where certain materials emit electrons when exposed to light is called
explanation: The photoelectric effect (discovered by Heinrich Hertz, explained by Einstein) is the emission of electrons from a material's surface when light of sufficient frequency (above the threshold frequency) strikes it.

text: According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons is
explanation: Einstein's photoelectric equation: KE_max = hf - W, where h is Planck's constant, f is the frequency of the incident light, and W (work function) is the minimum energy needed to remove an electron.

text: The nucleus of an atom consists of
explanation: The atomic nucleus contains protons (positively charged) and neutrons (no charge). Electrons orbit the nucleus in shells.

text: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom is called the
explanation: The atomic number (Z) is the number of protons in the nucleus. It identifies the element. The mass number (A) is the total number of protons and neutrons.

text: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with
explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number (same number of protons) but different mass numbers because they have different numbers of neutrons. E.g., Carbon-12 and Carbon-14.

text: The energy of a photon is given by
explanation: The energy of a photon E = hf, where h is Planck's constant (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ Js) and f is the frequency of the electromagnetic radiation.

text: Alpha particles are identical to the nucleus of which atom?
explanation: Alpha particles consist of 2 protons and 2 neutrons — identical to a helium-4 nucleus (₂⁴He). They have a charge of +2 and are relatively massive.

text: Which type of nuclear radiation has the greatest penetrating power?
explanation: Gamma rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiation with the greatest penetrating power. Alpha particles are stopped by paper, beta by a few mm of aluminium, but gamma requires several cm of lead to significantly attenuate.

text: Radioactive decay follows which type of mathematical relationship?
explanation: Radioactive decay follows exponential decay: N = N₀e^(-λt), where λ is the decay constant. The number of undecayed nuclei decreases exponentially with time.

text: The half-life of a radioactive substance is the time taken for
optionD: the substance to lose half its mass
explanation: Half-life (T½) is the time taken for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay. After each half-life, the activity reduces by half.

text: A radioactive substance has a half-life of 20 years. After 60 years, the fraction of the original sample remaining is
explanation: Number of half-lives = 60/20 = 3. Fraction remaining = (½)³ = 1/8.

text: Nuclear fission is the process in which
optionA: small nuclei combine to form a larger nucleus
optionB: a heavy nucleus splits into smaller nuclei
optionC: electrons are emitted from a nucleus
explanation: Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus (e.g. Uranium-235) into two smaller nuclei when struck by a neutron, releasing a large amount of energy.

text: Which of the following is used as a moderator in a nuclear reactor?
explanation: A moderator slows down fast neutrons to thermal (slow) speeds needed for fission. Heavy water (D₂O) and graphite are common moderators. Control rods (made of boron or cadmium) absorb neutrons.

text: In a p-n junction diode, conventional current flows
explanation: In a forward-biased p-n junction, conventional current (positive charge flow) moves from the p-type (anode) to the n-type (cathode) side through the diode.

text: Which of the following electronic components is used to amplify signals?
explanation: A transistor can be used as an amplifier. A small input signal at the base controls a larger current between collector and emitter, amplifying the signal.

text: In digital electronics, a logic gate that gives an output of 1 only when all inputs are 1 is the
explanation: The AND gate produces a HIGH (1) output only when ALL inputs are HIGH (1). Its boolean expression is Y = A·B.

text: Which logic gate produces an output that is the complement (opposite) of its input?
explanation: The NOT gate (inverter) produces the complement of its input: if input is 1, output is 0, and vice versa. Its boolean expression is Y = Ā.

text: A full-wave rectifier converts
optionB: AC to DC by using both halves of the cycle
optionC: AC to DC by using only one half of the cycle
explanation: A full-wave rectifier uses both the positive and negative halves of the AC cycle, producing a more complete DC output compared to a half-wave rectifier.

text: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
explanation: Solar energy is renewable because it comes from the Sun, which is an inexhaustible (on human timescales) source. Fossil fuels (coal, gas, petroleum) are non-renewable finite resources.

text: The type of energy conversion in a solar cell is
explanation: A solar cell (photovoltaic cell) converts light (solar) energy directly into electrical energy using the photovoltaic effect in semiconductor materials.

text: Which of the following energy sources causes the least environmental pollution?
explanation: Hydroelectric power generates electricity from flowing water with no direct carbon emissions or air pollution during operation, making it the cleanest option in the list.

text: The process by which the Sun generates its energy is
explanation: The Sun generates energy through nuclear fusion: hydrogen nuclei (protons) fuse together to form helium nuclei, releasing an enormous amount of energy according to E = mc².

text: Which of the following is NOT a form of energy?
explanation: Power is the rate of doing work (or transferring energy), not a form of energy itself. Kinetic, thermal and chemical energy are all genuine forms of energy.

text: Physics is best described as the study of
optionC: matter and energy and their interactions
explanation: Physics is the branch of natural science that studies matter, energy, and the fundamental forces of nature, and how they interact with each other.

text: Which of the following is a fundamental unit in the SI system?
explanation: The SI base units include the metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela. Newton, Joule and Pascal are derived units.

text: The instrument used to measure temperature is called a
explanation: A thermometer measures temperature. A barometer measures atmospheric pressure, a hygrometer measures humidity, and an anemometer measures wind speed.

text: Which of the following instruments is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure. Evangelista Torricelli invented the mercury barometer. Standard atmospheric pressure is approximately 101,325 Pa or 760 mmHg.

text: A simple machine is a device that
optionB: changes the speed of a body
optionC: makes work easier by changing the magnitude or direction of a force
explanation: A simple machine makes work easier. It can change the magnitude or direction of an applied force. Examples include levers, pulleys, inclined planes, screws and wheel-and-axle.

text: The mechanical advantage of a machine is defined as
optionA: output force divided by input force
optionB: input force divided by output force
optionC: output distance divided by input distance
explanation: Mechanical advantage (MA) = Load / Effort = output force / input force. A MA greater than 1 means the machine multiplies force.

text: Which class of lever has the effort between the fulcrum and the load?
explanation: In a third-class lever, the effort is applied between the fulcrum and the load. Examples include tweezers, fishing rods and the human forearm. These levers multiply distance/speed rather than force.

text: A pulley system with three supporting ropes (velocity ratio = 3) is used to lift a 300 N load. The effort required (assuming 100% efficiency) is
explanation: Effort = Load / Velocity Ratio = 300 / 3 = 100 N. With 100% efficiency, MA = VR, so Effort = Load/VR.

text: An inclined plane is used to slide a box of weight 600 N onto a truck 1.5 m high using a plank 3 m long. The effort needed (ignoring friction) is
explanation: VR = length/height = 3/1.5 = 2. Effort = Load/VR = 600/2 = 300 N. The inclined plane reduces the force needed but increases the distance over which it is applied.

text: Heat transfer by direct contact between particles of matter is called
explanation: Conduction is heat transfer through direct particle-to-particle contact. Metals are good conductors. Convection involves fluid movement; radiation requires no medium.

text: Which method of heat transfer can occur through a vacuum?
explanation: Radiation is the transfer of heat energy in the form of electromagnetic waves (infrared radiation). Unlike conduction and convection, it does not require a material medium and can travel through a vacuum.

text: The fixed temperature at which a pure substance changes from solid to liquid is called its
explanation: The melting point is the temperature at which a solid changes to a liquid at atmospheric pressure. For ice, the melting point is 0°C.

text: The specific heat capacity of a substance is
optionA: the heat needed to melt 1 kg of the substance
optionB: the heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg by 1°C
optionC: the heat released when 1 kg vaporises
optionD: the ratio of heat to volume
explanation: Specific heat capacity (c) is the amount of heat energy needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K (or 1°C). Q = mcΔT.

text: The absolute zero of temperature in Kelvin is
explanation: Absolute zero is 0 K, which equals -273.15°C. It is the lowest theoretically possible temperature, at which particles have minimum thermal energy.

text: Which of the following statements about mass and weight is CORRECT?
optionA: Mass changes with location; weight does not
optionB: Weight changes with location; mass does not
optionC: Both mass and weight change with location
optionD: Neither mass nor weight changes with location
explanation: Mass is a scalar quantity that is constant regardless of location. Weight (W = mg) depends on gravitational field strength (g), which varies with location (e.g. on the Moon g is about 1/6 of Earth's value).

text: A body is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of 20 m/s. The maximum height reached (g = 10 m/s²) is
explanation: At maximum height, v = 0. Using v² = u² - 2gh: 0 = 400 - 2(10)h → h = 400/20 = 20 m.

text: The gradient of a velocity-time graph gives
explanation: The gradient (slope) of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration. The area under the graph gives displacement.

text: A ticker tape shows 5 dots per centimetre. The frequency of the timer is 50 Hz. What is the time interval between each dot?
explanation: Period = 1/frequency = 1/50 = 0.02 s. This means the timer makes one dot every 0.02 seconds.

text: Which of the following is NOT a vector quantity?
explanation: Distance is a scalar quantity (magnitude only). Acceleration, momentum and displacement are all vector quantities (they have both magnitude and direction).

text: The base unit for length in the SI system is
explanation: The SI (International System of Units) base unit for length is the metre (m). Centimetre, millimetre and kilometre are multiples or sub-multiples of the metre.

text: The number of significant figures in the value 0.00450 is
explanation: In 0.00450, the leading zeros are not significant (they only locate the decimal point). The significant figures are 4, 5 and 0 (the trailing zero after the 5 is significant). So there are 3 significant figures.

text: A vernier caliper has a main scale reading of 2.3 cm and a vernier scale reading of 0.04 cm. The actual reading is
explanation: The total reading = main scale reading + vernier scale reading = 2.3 + 0.04 = 2.34 cm.

text: The turning effect of a force about a pivot is called
explanation: The moment (torque) of a force about a pivot is the product of the force and its perpendicular distance from the pivot. M = F × d. Its SI unit is Nm.

text: The principle of moments states that for a body in equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments
optionC: equals the sum of anti-clockwise moments
explanation: The principle of moments (for a body in rotational equilibrium): sum of clockwise moments = sum of anti-clockwise moments about any point.

text: Which of the following correctly defines impulse?
explanation: Impulse = Force × time = Ft. It equals the change in momentum of the object (Ft = mv - mu). Its SI unit is Ns (Newton-second).

text: The law of conservation of momentum states that the total momentum of a system of bodies
optionC: remains constant provided no external force acts
optionD: depends on the type of collision
explanation: The law of conservation of linear momentum: in a closed system (no external net force), total momentum before = total momentum after a collision or interaction.

text: What is the velocity ratio of a single fixed pulley?
explanation: A single fixed pulley has a velocity ratio of 1. It does not multiply force — it only changes the direction of the applied force, making pulling downward easier than lifting upward.

text: Heat energy required to change 2 kg of ice at 0°C to water at 0°C (latent heat of fusion of ice = 3.36 × 10⁵ J/kg) is
explanation: Q = mL = 2 × 3.36 × 10⁵ = 6.72 × 10⁵ J. The latent heat of fusion is energy absorbed during melting at constant temperature.

text: The loudness of sound is measured in
explanation: The loudness (intensity level) of sound is measured in decibels (dB). Frequency is measured in Hertz (Hz).

text: Visible light is part of the electromagnetic spectrum. Which colour has the highest frequency?
explanation: In the visible spectrum, violet light has the highest frequency (and shortest wavelength), while red has the lowest frequency (and longest wavelength). ROYGBIV order goes from red (lowest frequency) to violet (highest frequency).

text: The power of a lens is measured in
explanation: The power of a lens P = 1/f, where f is the focal length in metres. The unit of lens power is the dioptre (D).

text: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
explanation: The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s (exactly 299,792,458 m/s). This is denoted by 'c'.

text: Which of the following best describes the process of nuclear fusion?
optionA: A heavy nucleus splitting into smaller parts
optionB: Two light nuclei combining to form a heavier nucleus
explanation: Nuclear fusion is the joining of two light nuclei (e.g. hydrogen isotopes deuterium and tritium) to form a heavier nucleus. It releases enormous energy and is the process powering the Sun.

text: The binding energy per nucleon is greatest for which element?
explanation: Iron-56 has the highest binding energy per nucleon (~8.8 MeV), making it the most stable nucleus. Elements lighter than iron release energy by fusion; heavier elements release energy by fission.

text: In a NPN transistor used as a switch or amplifier, the three terminals are
explanation: A bipolar junction transistor (BJT) has three terminals: emitter, base and collector. In an NPN transistor, a small current into the base controls a larger current from collector to emitter.

text: Which gate has the truth table where output is 0 only when all inputs are 1?
explanation: The NAND gate is the complement of the AND gate. Its output is LOW (0) only when ALL inputs are HIGH (1). For all other input combinations, the output is HIGH (1).

text: The process of superimposing information signals onto a carrier wave is called
explanation: Modulation is the process of varying a property (amplitude, frequency or phase) of a high-frequency carrier wave in accordance with a lower-frequency information signal for transmission purposes.

text: Which of the following correctly defines the term 'work function' in photoelectric emission?
optionA: The maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons
optionB: The minimum energy required to remove an electron from a metal surface
optionC: The energy of the incident photon
optionD: The frequency threshold of incident light
explanation: The work function (W or φ) is the minimum energy needed to liberate an electron from the surface of a metal. It varies for different metals. The threshold frequency f₀ = W/h.

text: An atom has atomic number 11 and mass number 23. How many neutrons does it have?
explanation: Number of neutrons = Mass number - Atomic number = 23 - 11 = 12. This is sodium (Na), with 11 protons, 12 neutrons and 11 electrons.

text: The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is approximately 1/6 that on Earth. If a man weighs 600 N on Earth, his weight on the Moon is
explanation: Weight on Moon = mg_moon = mg_earth/6 = 600/6 = 100 N. His mass remains 60 kg but his weight changes because gravitational field strength is different.

text: A stone of mass 0.5 kg is dropped from a height of 20 m. What is its speed just before hitting the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: Using energy conservation: ½mv² = mgh → v = √(2gh) = √(2 × 10 × 20) = √400 = 20 m/s. Alternatively, v² = 2gh.

text: Which of the following is an example of potential energy being converted to kinetic energy?
optionB: A ball falling from a height
explanation: As a ball falls, its gravitational potential energy (mgh) is progressively converted into kinetic energy (½mv²). At the point of impact, almost all PE has become KE (ignoring air resistance).

text: The frequency range of sounds audible to a normal human ear is approximately
explanation: The normal human hearing range is approximately 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz (20 kHz). Sounds below 20 Hz are infrasound; above 20,000 Hz are ultrasound.

text: Ultrasonics are used in
explanation: Ultrasound (frequencies above 20,000 Hz) is used in medical ultrasound scanning (sonography) to image internal organs, in sonar for submarine detection and in non-destructive testing of materials.

text: The pressure at a depth h in a liquid of density ρ is given by
explanation: Pressure due to a column of liquid: P = ρgh, where ρ is the liquid density (kg/m³), g is gravitational acceleration (m/s²) and h is the depth (m).

text: A gas occupies 500 cm³ at a pressure of 100 kPa. At constant temperature, what volume will it occupy at 250 kPa?
explanation: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ at constant temperature. V₂ = P₁V₁/P₂ = (100 × 500)/250 = 200 cm³.

text: The device used to measure the electromotive force (EMF) of a cell accurately is a
explanation: A potentiometer measures EMF accurately because it draws no current from the source being measured (null deflection method). A voltmeter has finite resistance and causes a slight current to flow, giving a slightly lower reading.

text: When light travels from a less dense to a more dense medium, it
optionA: speeds up and bends away from the normal
optionB: slows down and bends towards the normal
optionC: slows down and bends away from the normal
optionD: speeds up and bends towards the normal
explanation: When light enters a denser medium, it slows down and bends towards the normal (angle of refraction < angle of incidence). Snell's law: n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂.

text: The unit of radioactivity (rate of decay) is the
explanation: The SI unit of radioactivity (number of decays per second) is the Becquerel (Bq). 1 Bq = 1 decay per second. The older unit is the Curie (Ci), where 1 Ci = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq.

text: In which direction does the force on a positive charge moving to the right in a magnetic field directed into the page act?
explanation: Using Fleming's right-hand rule (or F = qv × B): velocity is to the right (+x), B is into the page (-z). F = q(v × B) = q(+x × -z) = q(+y) = upward direction.
